text: Lagrange's theorem states that for a finite group G with a subgroup H ≤ G:
choices: every divisor of |G| is the order of some subgroup of G
G has a subgroup of every prime order
explanation: Lagrange's theorem says the order of a subgroup divides the order of the group, |H| | |G|, proved by partitioning G into cosets of equal size |H|. Option B reverses the divisibility. Options C and D assert forms of the (false) converse of Lagrange — A₄ has order 12 but no subgroup of order 6.
